newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end flat in mixed trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end flat in mixed trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed almost unchanged on Wednesday in mixed and balanced trading, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.04 percent, or 0.10 points, to 263.87 on an all-share turnover of 118 million shekels against 138 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.08 percent higher at 272.33.

"The market was very quiet today. It made a big move on Tuesday (rising 1.5 percent) and now it needs to stabilise before it can resume its rise," said Ilan Doron head of trading at Solid Capital Markets.
"Trading was very mixed and selective. It is only normal that after several positive sessions the market relaxes," said Michael Wiess at Evergreen Capital Markets.

"The market is very healthy and it looks good. The fact that the market is rising slowly and gradually is very positive. The good news is that yields on unlinked bonds are declining and in the long term money will start moving into the stock market as well," Doron said.
Traders noted that the market was not affected by forecasts of a relatively high April consumer price index of 1.1 percent. The CPI will be released on Thursday after the end of the trading day.

American Israeli Paper Mills gained 1.0 percent to 14,280 agorot. The company said on Wednesday that net profit in the first quarter of 1997 fell to 12.5 million shekels from 13.8 million shekels in the same period last year.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 0.5 percent to 19,371 agorot on turnover of 7.7 million shekels; Discount Investments, which surged 4.0 percent to 27,624 on volume of 6.9 million shekels and traders said there was no known reason for the surge; and Israel Chemicals, which lost 0.5 percent to 393 agorot on turnover of 4.2 million shekels.
